native_result.query: What proportion of studies in Experimental Economics were conducted in a lab setting?
native_result.HypoA: In Experimental Economics, all studies (both original and replication) were conducted in a lab setting (100%), while in Psychology, a small proportion of replication studies were also conducted online (8.8%)
native_result.HypoB: Filtering the study-level meta-regression data to the Experimental Economics replication project (project == "ee") gives 18 original studies (18 O/R pairs, one row per id, so per-study and per-pair counts coincide at 18). Summarizing online.o (original experiment conducted online: 1 = yes, 0 = no) over those 18 rows shows 18 with online.o == 0 and none with online.o == 1, so 18/18 = 100% of Experimental Economics original studies were conducted in an in-person lab setting; online.o is constant at 0 within ee, so this is a boundary (ceiling) value. No EE original study used an online sample, so lab-based administration is effectively universal in this replication set; this is corroborated by compensation.o == "cash" for all 18 and by online.r == 0 / same_online == 1 for all 18. Caveats from the same dataset: only 17/18 (~94%) used student subject pools (subjects.o == "students"; the single exception, ee.4 "Participation", used community subjects but was still an offline session), and only 11/18 (~61%) were US-based labs (us_lab.o == 1, which is identical to experiment_country.o == "United States" and therefore a US-location flag rather than a lab-vs-field indicator). lab_id is replication-lab identity and is 100% missing for ee, so it was excluded.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Loaded data/meta-regression_study_data_heterogeneity_in_replication_projects.csv (927 x 57) and confirmed all setting-relevant columns. 2) Filtered project == "ee" -> 18 rows = 18 unique ids = 18 distinct original studies (per-study == per-pair; no duplicate handling needed; ml1/ml3 aggregated-vs-per-lab duplication does not affect ee; drop filter not applied since all ee rows are drop == False). 3) Checked NA in the operative variable online.o (0 NA, so no exclusion and denominator stays 18) and confirmed online.o has zero variance (all 0) in ee. 4) Headline proportion = count(online.o == 0)/18 = 18/18 = 100% (boundary/ceiling value). 5) Pre-registered sensitivity ladder computed with numerator/denominator: online.o == 0 -> 18/18; online.o == 0 & subjects.o == 'students' -> 17/18; subjects.o == 'students' -> 17/18; us_lab.o == 1 -> 11/18 (US-location flag only, verified identical to experiment_country.o == 'United States'). 6) Descriptive block for ee: subjects.o mix (students 17, community 1), compensation.o (cash 18/18), experiment_country.o distribution, online.r == 0 and same_online == 1 for all 18, lab_id 0/18 populated. 7) Confirmed the replication-success dataset (143 x 15) has no setting/lab field and was not used. Scripts: analysis/inspect_01.py, analysis/inspect_02.py, analysis/compute_lab_prop.py with matching *_output.txt logs and analysis/lab_setting_summary.json.
